key_agent_trends: Major funding flows into agent infrastructure: LangChain at $3B valuation and Mirendil's $1B Series A highlight investor confidence in tools that govern and automate AI research and deployment.
Agentic commerce advances with OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet enabling secure, biometric-approved purchases by Dots agents using tokenized payments.
Enterprises demand control: Anthropic opens self-hosted Claude Managed Agents beta so companies can run agent harnesses and data on their own infrastructure.
Production scale demonstrated by AT&T running nearly 500 agentic workflows, processing massive token volumes and planning to triple capacity.
Open-source agent tooling expands as Cloudflare releases Kitesurf browser engine under Apache 2.0 for efficient, scalable agent web interactions.

stories.headline: LangChain raises $300 million Series C at $3 billion valuation
stories.what_happened: On November 13, 2026, LangChain announced a $300 million Series C led by CapitalG at a $3 billion valuation, more than double its previous mark. The round included GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP, Sapphire Ventures and others. LangSmith, its platform for running, evaluating and governing agents, now serves over 7,000 organizations including Harvey, NVIDIA and Salesforce.
stories.why_it_matters: It signals strong demand for model-neutral agent infrastructure that lets enterprises own and control their agent deployments rather than relying solely on model providers.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet so Dots agents can make secure purchases
stories.what_happened: On November 13, 2026, OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Wallet, built with American Express, Mastercard and Visa. It lets Dots agents complete purchases after user review and biometric approval such as Face ID, using payment tokens so agents never see actual card details. Initial rollout is limited to US ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18+ with eligible cards.
stories.why_it_matters: It establishes a practical, secure path for agentic commerce while preserving user control and existing card protections, accelerating real-world agent transactions.

stories.headline: Anthropic opens private beta for self-hosted Claude Managed Agents
stories.what_happened: On November 12, 2026, Anthropic launched a private beta of self-hosted Claude Managed Agents. Companies can run the full agent harness, PostgreSQL database, sandboxes, credentials and session history in their own cloud or on-premises, while model calls go to Anthropic, Bedrock, Google, Foundry or a custom gateway. Access is requested via account teams.
stories.why_it_matters: It addresses enterprise needs for data residency, security and control over agent infrastructure without requiring full model self-hosting.

stories.headline: Mirendil raises $1 billion Series A to automate AI research with agents
stories.what_happened: On November 12, 2026, Mirendil announced a $1 billion Series A led by Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital, with participation from Google and others. The company builds tools including Lor, which runs hundreds of agents to write code and run experiments. It reported that one researcher with agents pretrained a competitive coding model from scratch in 3.5 months for under $10 million in compute.
stories.why_it_matters: It demonstrates how agents can compress the cost and team size required for frontier AI development, accelerating research accessibility.

stories.headline: AT&T runs nearly 500 agentic AI workflows in production, plans to triple them
stories.what_happened: AT&T reported nearly 500 agentic workflows already in production, handling more than 1 million transactions monthly and processing about 45 billion AI tokens daily. The company plans to triple the number next year. Workflows cover areas such as customer provisioning and sales prospecting, with the Business Agent Foundry redesigning processes around agents.
stories.why_it_matters: It provides a concrete large-enterprise example of agentic AI moving from pilots to scaled production operations with measurable volume.

stories.headline: Cloudflare open-sources Kitesurf, its lightweight browser engine for AI agents
stories.what_happened: On November 13, 2026, Cloudflare released the source code for Kitesurf under the Apache 2.0 license on GitHub. Kitesurf is a stateless browser that runs entirely on Cloudflare Workers, parsing HTML, applying CSS, executing JavaScript and rendering without a full Chromium container. It supports the Chrome DevTools Protocol and is designed for lower CPU and memory use by agents.
stories.why_it_matters: Open-sourcing an efficient agent browser lowers barriers for developers building computer-use and web-interaction agents and encourages customization.
